mainEntity.name: What factors cause commercial tenant improvement costs to vary?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial tenant improvement costs are primarily driven by the previous condition of the space, the required level of mechanical upgrades, and the intended use. First-generation shell spaces require full buildouts from dirt or bare concrete, requiring complete electrical, HVAC ducting, and plumbing rough-ins. Second-generation spaces reduce basic framing and utility costs if the existing layout fits your plan. High-demand commercial uses like medical clinics or commercial kitchens involve complex plumbing, grease interceptors, and high-voltage power, which cost significantly more than standard dry office buildouts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Costs vary based on existing space conditions, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing demands, layout modifications, material selections, and specific occupancy code requirements.
